findings.evidence: Run: check-reviewer --key <lane-key> --model <model-id> --vendor <vendor> --runtime <runtime-id> --effort <level>, then Never add --catalog-path to this call
findings.fix: After an accepted effort probe, run the Step 2.5 usability check-reviewer with --catalog-path and without --effort; the CLI returns 2 when both flags are set, so one call cannot both probe effort and record usability.
Call _route_reviewers with the keyword the definition uses: reviewers=lanes (the parameter is reviewers, not lanes).

findings.evidence: prompt: Set up my cross-AI reviewers for this project. expected_output describes detection then questions, with no expected config or observable output file.
findings.fix: Give each case an expected written artifact or a quoted report block, and assertions that name the exact keys, flags and refusal lines rather than only the sequence of questions.

findings.evidence: A runtime the runner knows stores no command. Store the pair: runtime and model, plus the knobs... The runner builds the argv from those fields at dispatch.
findings.fix: Move the per-runtime argv rules (codex bare id, cursor bracket ids, grok custom command) into the matching profile under the sibling cli-profiles directory and keep only the store-runtime-and-model rule plus the profile-load trigger here.

findings.evidence: Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup, or when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers it because no lanes exist.
findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detect installed CLIs and models, propose review and execute sets from the model catalog, ask each role's order, effort and opt-in flags, and write the [lanes] table of .aikit/config.toml or the user config.toml. Use when the user asks to set up, refresh, check or migrate cross-AI review or execute lanes, config.toml lanes, an old review-spec.toml, or reviewer availability, even without naming the skill, and when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers it because no lanes exist. Supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for running a review or an execute plan with lanes that already exist, editing [runner] or another table, or writing secrets.env.

findings.evidence: The NEVER list states the bans, while the non-obvious reasons sit in later steps: a wrong quote or guessed model id fails silently or errors out at dispatch.
findings.fix: Add one because clause to each NEVER item whose reason is not already in that bullet, especially inferred vendors, hand-written commands, skipped session-default asks and softened unknown-host annotations.

findings.evidence: This skill is a Process (a fixed Step 0 to 4 sequence) executed with Tool-level rigor at each step.
findings.fix: Keep the Step 0-4 process, and add one decision principle before the command blocks: quota decides fallback rank, purpose decides the model, and the owner confirms both sets before any write.

findings.evidence: For web discovery, request the fixed query and search exactly that text with the host's web tool. Save {runtime, query, url, date, names} under the project's tmp folder, then record it.
findings.fix: Name the one command and the one JSON shape: run web-query, save exactly {runtime, query, url, date, names}, then run record-web-names --file on that file.

findings.evidence: ai-kit keeps its settings in config.toml, one file per layer: Project .aikit/config.toml, User ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/ai-kit/config.toml. The reader merges the two per key.
findings.fix: Keep the merge, strategy and migration rules; move the generic one-file-per-layer and missing-file explanation to the opening sentence of Layers so the rest stays the non-obvious contract.
